headline: Approved the DPW garage and fleet maintenance facility and 14 other items in a draft capital bond plan, and adopted draft bonding guidance.
summary: The committee reviewed a draft plan listing approved, unauthorized, and unprogrammed capital projects, with debt service projections for future bond sales. Members approved items 13 through 26 of the plan, then approved item 12, the DPW garage and fleet maintenance facility, with Alderwoman Kelly abstaining. The committee also adopted the draft guidance.
decisions: Approved items 13 through 26 of the draft G.O. bond plan. Motion carried.
Approved item 12, the DPW garage and fleet maintenance facility, as part of the plan. Motion carried, with Alderwoman Kelly abstaining.
Adopted the draft guidance on bond authorizations, capital spending, and debt sales. Motion carried.

AD HOC JOINT COMMITTEE ON CAPITAL EXPENDITURES AND DEBT SERVICE PLANNING 
   
AUGUST 10, 2026 
 
 
A meeting of the Ad Hoc Joint Committee on Capital Expenditures and Debt Service Planning was held Monday, 
August 10, 2026, at 6:00 p.m. in the aldermanic chamber, and duly noticed in two places, including the City’s 
website, in accordance with the requirements of RSA 91-A:2 II.   
 
Let’s start the meeting by taking a roll call attendance.  If you are participating via Zoom, please state your presence, 
reason for not attending the meeting in person, and whether there is anyone in the room with you during this meeting, 
which is required under the Right-To-Know Law. 
 
The roll call was taken with 7 members of the Ad Hoc Joint Committee present:   
 
Mayor James Donchess, Chairman, presided. 
 
Members of the Committee present: Mayor James Donch ess 
 Alderman-at-Large Lori Wilshire 
 Alderwoman-at-Large Shoshanna Kelly 
 Alderman Patricia Klee 
 Tim Cummings, Administrative Services Director 
 Lisa Fauteux, Public Works Director  
 Matt Sullivan, Community Development Director 
  
Members of the Committee absent: Alderman-at-Large Ben Clemons  
  
Also in attendance:   Alderman Paula Johnson   
           
 
ROLL CALL 
 
DISCUSSION 
 
 
 Draft Updated Plan 
 
 
Tim Cummings, Administrative Services Director 
 
Again for the record, Tim Cummings, Director of Administrative Services.  So for this evening, I'd like to walk 
through the plan as it's been developed to date and then walk you through the work that our finance team has 
done to show how the plan corresponds and correlates with previous guidance that have been given by the Board 
of Aldermen and the Committee in in the past.  The ultimate goal is to try to get to some sort of consensus this 
evening as I'd like to present to the Board of Aldermen tomorrow night and then ultimately what we really need to 
do is file bond resolutions for the September meeting. So we are really starting to cut it tight.  
 
So you'll see a couple handouts were on the table.  Hopefully everyone has received them.  Essentially, they are 
the outline that I'll go through from the PowerPoint this evening and the various charts and graphs that we will go 
over in in detail.  
 
So just as a reminder, previous guidance and we're continuing forward with these recommendations is to file our 
bond resolutions concurrently or right after the fiscal year operational budget.  Capital improvement spending 
through the operating budget - we're in and around $1.5 million right now.  We're looking to increase the 
appropriately year over year to try to increase our cash we use for various capital projects.  Previous guidance 
was limit new debt sales to approximately $25 million a year using a $25 million average over a five-year period 
plus inflationary factor.  I'll note this is something we may want to go over and talk about depending on what the 
body's priorities are.  Authorize additional spending with surplus through supplemental appropriation in that fall 
time period.  
 
Lastly, I just want to note this is something I brought up at the last meeting but I do think it's worth reiterating 
again is any discussion about the plan before us is going to require us exempting debt from the cap calculation.  
So that's something that has been done in years past.  I think it's going to be something that we're going to need 
to do again to be able to adhere to the various financial constraints that we have before us.
Ad Hoc Capital/Debt Committee – 08/10/2026                                                                         Page 2 
   
 
So with that being said, I'd like to call your attention to the handouts that have been provided to you.  I originally 
provided you this geo bonding plan at the last meeting.  I provided that draft to you, and I solicited input, and I 
heard some commentary about some changes and tweaks that you'd like to see.  So I've updated the plan 
accordingly.  I'm going to go through line by line and talk about these changes and also make some editorial 
comments for you to keep in the back of your mind depending on what your priorities may be.  There may be 
ways to potentially drive our planning projects down from a five-year average perspective or increase it depending 
on what your pleasure may be.  
 
So starting off just at the top, we have approved resolutions with bond authorization where we are selling the 
debt.  First is the continuing our general paving… 
 
Chairman Donchess 
 
Let me just interrupt for a moment.  The record should show that Alderwoman Johnson has arrived. 
 
Alderman Johnson 
 
Thank you. 
 
Tim Cummings, Administrative Services Director 
 
So again right at the top here, we have approved resolutions with bond authorizations, and we need to sell the 
debt, and so first, we have continuing the general paving program.  This was originally done in 2022 for $37.5 
million dollars.  We have expended almost all of that.  We have about $7.5 million still to spend over the next two 
years and it's accommodated appropriately.  
 
Next, we have the infrastructure - general infrastructure improvement of Walnut Street and the West Pearl Street.  
The Walnut Street oval and the West Pearl Street Streetscaping Project and so we have some debt still to sell on 
that project and that's noted in FY27.  
 
We have the parking garages - both High and Elm Street parking garages.  Originally a $15 million bond 
authorization.  We have about $3 million of debt still to sell.   
 
Continuing on that West Pearl Street Streetscaping and Walnut Street Oval Project, we have about $600,000 of 
debt still to sell in a separate authorization.   
 
We have the DPW garage and fleet maintenance facility project where we are authorized $3 million and we 
anticipate selling that at least $2 million this year and a million dollars next year.  
 
Library design.  We have $1 million authorized and anticipate selling $1 million.  
 
Citywide infrastructure signal implementation project.  We have a million dollars authorized, and I believe we will 
be spending that in a couple years from now, and it's slated to come up in FY29.  
 
Holman Stadium.  Total project cost is, I believe, something like $7 million. We've authorized three and we have 
anticipated that debt to be sold in FY29 and FY30.  
 
Then moving on to unauthorized debt and programmed in the over the next five to six or so years.  You can see 
here we have the DPW garage and fleet maintenance facility for $43.5 million dollars and it is outlined 
accordingly.  
 
We have the fire general deferred capital maintenance program.  This would be reoccurring deferred capital 
maintenance that needs to be spent of about $1.5 million.  
 
We have schools needing deferred capital maintenance.  It's programmed in here at $2 million.   
 
As I noted above, the general paving program is coming to an end so we need to reauthorize it.  I have it 
programmed in here at $4 million starting in in FY29, which aligns with the current debt service planning that
Ad Hoc Capital/Debt Committee – 08/10/2026                                                                         Page 3 
   
we've done in the past.  
 
We have CERF that we need to continue to accommodate and so we have CERF needing $4 million to bring us 
up to current spending levels not to account for additional spending that we anticipate.   
 
We have a library renovation project of $44 million.  That doesn't count the $1 million that's already been noted 
above.  Total project cost of $45 million.  
 
Fire training facility of $1.5 million and then a fire station rehab or what's known as the “Pine Hill Station Number 
5” for $35 million happening a couple years out.  
 
We have another, again, the continuation of the Holman Stadium project of $4 million dollars and that's happening 
out after ‘31, I believe, and out into ‘32.  
 
The City of Nashua needs to update our ERP system for $10 million dollars and that is spread out accordingly.  
 
And then we have a new addition of prior comment heard that we needed to increase how much we had set aside 
for the pools, and we added $5 million for the pools, and that needs to be done sooner rather than later, and it is 
noted to come up in FY27 for $3 million.  
 
Hydro improvements.  This is the regulatory requirements only for $15 million dollars.  We have that programmed 
as well and added into the plan.  
 
And then finally, we have the cell block for the Police Department at $3 million added into the plan, but it's in later 
in the in the schedule and coming up in FY32.  
 
Citywide infrastructure improvements, again, pedestrian bridge.  We have a contractual obligation to do this but 
the money is not necessary until an outer year so I accommodated it in FY33, which tracks along the lines of 
where we believe it is necessary.  That is all unauthorized debt but programmed that we anticipate potentially 
doing capital projects on over the next five or so year horizon.   
 
Unprogrammed and unauthorized.   just to note, I included it on the bottom here is the resource center where I 
believe some additional community input is necessary before we can proceed.  I know there's going to be a 
discussion about a school parking lot being needed at some point in the future.  We also have the hydro 
improvements that are the non-regulatory improvements.  We don't have a dollar amount associated to it just yet, 
but we do know it's a program that's on the horizon.  We have a citywide car wash necessary just approximately 
$3 million.  General school renovation.  We know there's going to be a need for a general school renovation.  We 
have a placeholder of $30 million there. Keefe Auditorium.  We don't have a number associated to this yet, but we 
know it's under active planning and so I anticipate a presentation to the Board of Aldermen in the near future 
where this could be discussed.  Then we have some other infrastructure projects that have been talked about 
from time to time but is, again, unprogrammed and unauthorized.  14 Court Street, the Court Street Theater, 
Riverside athletic fields, a new fire station, and then a passenger rail station being necessary.   
 
So with that being said, everything that's in the approved and the unauthorized but blue categories, the average 
five year is about $39 million.  We should be spending on average about $30 million so we're a little high.  I think 
there's some ways we could potentially tweak this to bring this down if that is the pleasure of the body but I 
wanted to just at least at this time report to you on the work that we've done to date.  
 
At this time, I'd like to hand it over to CFO Enwright who can talk to you about how we can accommodate this debt 
on the various schedules she's provided to you this evening.  So if I could, Mr. Mayor, I'd like to hand it over to 
CFO Enwright. 
 
Chairman Donchess 
 
Yes, please. 
 
Dawn Enwright, CFO 
 
Thank you.  For the record, Dawn Enwright, CFO.  So first, I'd like to draw your attention to the spreadsheet at the
Ad Hoc Capital/Debt Committee – 08/10/2026                                                                         Page 4 
   
top that says “target bonded debt service projects”.  This schedule that's in front of you is looking at what the 
target plan was agreed upon last year, which is the $25 million dollars starting in 2025 with a 5 percent inflationary 
increase year over year and what the debt would look like if we stayed in line with the target plan.  So for instance 
in 2027, the target amount was $27,562 500 and so forth.  What I would like to do - oh, the current debt column is 
what we currently are paying our debt service on today.  That is the current debt service.

to try to decide what are the priorities within the $25 million a year guideline that had previously been established.  
So, the point of this is to try to arrive at a plan that hits that guideline of $25 million a year.   
 
What does $25 million if we have a 4% interest rate?  That's about a million dollars a year, plus the principle, but a 
million dollars impacts the tax rate.  I'm just giving you some ballpark figures.  About, you know, one quarter to 
one - 1/3 to 40%, you know, of a 1/3 to .4% of a percentage on the tax rate. Now that does not take into account

inform you further.  
 
Dawn Enwright, CFO 
 
Thank you.  
 
Chairman Donchess

I just wanted to also clarify for historical purposes the CIC grade to the right of that might be helpful for the
